newsitem.title: USA: First Union holders mulling options.
newsitem.headline: First Union holders mulling options.

text.p: A group including Gotham Partners, a New York-based investment firm, said Monday it may seek to change control of First Union Real Estate Equity and Mortgage Investments.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the investors said they will continuously assess the company's business and financial condition and may opt to "actively influence" the company's management by, among other things, seeking a new slate of directors and managers.

"The reporting persons believe that the company has significant unrealized equity potential which can be realized if the company is able to execute a substantial number of sizable acquisitions," the investors, who hold the equivalent of a 6.7 percent stake or 1.9 million shares, said in the SEC filing.
Further, the investors said they may try to push the Cleveland-based real estate investment company into merging with another business or reorganizing.

The investors most recently bought 721,700 common shares between April 11 and June 10 at prices ranging from $12.78 to $13.91 a share. The group's holdings also include options to acquire common shares.
